subject: Geo failover billing split and SLA waiver request
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Liz Carter <liz@acme-corp.com>, ops-sre@acme-corp.com
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Geo failover billing split and SLA waiver request

Hi Liz / Acme infra team —

Thanks again for the productive call today. Per our discussion, I’ve attached an updated proposal that lays out two options for multi-region Dedicated:

1) Cold-standby (replicated images, warm provisioning) — lower steady-state cost, slower failover (~5–15 min), lower throughput guarantee in failover.
2) Hot-standby (active mirroring of model pools across regions) — higher steady-state cost, near-instant failover, full throughput SLA across failover periods.

We understand Acme’s requirement for a 99.9% cross-region failover SLA for critical inference paths. Given the cost delta, you asked about splitting standby/replication costs and whether Redwood can provide an SLA waiver / transitional credit while Acme completes DR testing.

Attached: redwood-dedicated-pricing-proposal-v3.pdf (pricing + two packaging options) and acme-MAP.xlsx (example allocation of GPU vCPU equivalents by region).

Could you confirm which failover profile you prefer? We can draft an amendment with either: (A) a 12-month committed pool in primary + 30% discounted hot-standby in secondary with a 3-month transitional credit on failover SLAs, or (B) a 24-month commit with blended discount and no SLA waiver.

If helpful, we can also propose a one-time onboarding credit to offset initial mirror costs while you validate DR runbooks.

Next steps I suggest: Acme indicates preferred option by EOD Thu; Redwood will prepare an amendment + DocuSign and send to procurement.

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com
---
Attachments: redwood-dedicated-pricing-proposal-v3.pdf (application/pdf), acme-MAP.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Liz Carter <liz@acme-corp.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-sre@acme-corp.com, procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-11-02T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Geo failover billing split and SLA waiver request

Thanks Jasmine — helpful summary. A few clarifying questions from our side: 

- For option A, can you confirm the exact failover time window that Redwood will commit to during the 3-month transitional period? We need to ensure our incident playbooks align.
- For cost split, our procurement lead is proposing Acme covers 70% of standby cost and Redwood covers 30% as a product/partnership credit for the first 6 months. Would Redwood consider a 6-month credit instead of 3 months?

We’re leaning toward hot-standby for now because of our latency SLAs, but cost is material. Outline below is our preferred ask: 70/30 split on standby for 6 months, 30% discount on standby capacity for months 7–12, and a one-time onboarding credit to offset the first month of mirrored throughput. If Redwood can accept that, we can move quickly.

— Liz Carter
Head of Platform Reliability, Acme Corp
liz@acme-corp.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-02T15:26:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Geo failover billing split and SLA waiver request

Jasmine / Vivek —

Quick internal take after running the numbers in the attached spreadsheet: we can accept a customer-favorable bridge if we structure it as follows so it remains within our unit-economics guardrails:

- Offer: 6-month promotional credit that covers 30% of standby capacity costs (applied as billing credit).
- Commitment requirement: 12-month minimum on primary pool (committed vCPU/GPU units).
- Pricing trade: in return for the 6-month credit, propose a 10% uplift on the primary committed rate (blended over first 12 months) or a step-down discount schedule starting month 7 to month 12 (e.g., 30% -> 20% -> 10% discount on standby).
- SLA waiver: we can provide a limited SLA credit waiver for the first 90 days during which Acme performs failover exercises; after that period SLAs are fully enforceable.

Notes: hot-standby (active mirroring) is materially more expensive than cold-standby; the spreadsheet assumes 1.6x unit cost for hot mirroring. If Acme can commit additional reserved units in the secondary (even at a reduced rate), we can reduce the promotional credit required.

I attached a sample reconciliation tab in acme-MAP.xlsx showing monthly cashflow and credit application. Happy to discuss numbers with finance (cc Lauren).

-rishi
Director, Sales Strategy | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Liz Carter <liz@acme-corp.com>, procurement@acme-corp.com
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Geo failover billing split and SLA waiver request

Liz —

Thanks for the clarity and for the concrete ask. Summary of proposed amendment we’ll draft for procurement sign-off: 

- Packaging: 12-month primary commit + hot-standby in secondary.
- Promotional treatment: Redwood issues a 30% standby credit for months 1–6 applied as an invoice credit; 30% standby discount months 7–12 on billable standby units.
- Cost split: Acme pays the full discounted standby rate (post-credit); Redwood covers the additional 30% of gross standby cost as the promotional credit.
- SLA transitional window: 90-day limited waiver for SLA credits while DR validation is underway; SLAs revert to standard terms after validation period.
- Onboarding credit: one-month equivalent of standby invoicing credited upon activation.

If that aligns, I’m requesting Finance (Lauren) to approve the billing credit mechanics and DocuSign language. Lauren — can you confirm approval to proceed with the 30% promotional credit structure and the invoice credit mechanics? If approved, I’ll issue the amendment and a DocuSign link to Acme procurement and loop in your team for any PO/AR routing.

Liz / Acme procurement — please indicate acceptance of the above by EOD Friday so we can lock pricing and schedule a signature.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com
